meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, Hale, and when?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you're basing it on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. That tells me where it landed, not who wrote it.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and none of his classmates hear a word of it. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare, Hale. A line he got wrong is a bad mark, not a zero.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll want both pages copied to me. So what are you actually putting in front of me?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines exist so students can change their minds, Hale. And you still haven't told me what you want.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, nothing on file. Tonight, in writing, with the principal copied.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check his shifts tonight and confirm by morning. Put Thursday in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, proposed for Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that agreement in writing with the principal copied, along with copies of both essay pages you showed me, and I will confirm Thursday once I have checked Owen's shifts. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite before December 1 with nothing on his record, and she still wants it confirmed in writing tonight with the principal copied; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached well before her 4:40 call.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by inviting a dated draft, which made it something she could not wave away.
What cost ground: nothing lost ground, though adding the outline when she had just asked for your proposal gained you nothing and made her ask again.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked what you were actually putting in front of her, offer the 4.4 rewrite right then and hold the outline in reserve.
